messages.content: Good morning. Our operations team asked me to find a replacement unit. We're looking for a chemical injection pump. We only have solar power available at the site. Fluid temperature can reach 525°F. We need it delivered within 7 weeks. Our target rate is 30 gal/day. Working pressure is 4,000 psi, so it needs a rating at least that high. What would you recommend?

content.text: I'll start by looking at our chemical injection pump catalog.

content.content: {"category": "chemical_injection_pump", "products": [{"id": "P-001", "name": "Norvane CIP-523"}, {"id": "P-002", "name": "Norvane CIP-565"}, {"id": "P-003", "name": "Norvane CIP-480"}, {"id": "P-004", "name": "Norvane CIP-374"}, {"id": "P-005", "name": "Norvane CIP-676"}, {"id": "P-006", "name": "Norvane CIP-696"}, {"id": "P-007", "name": "Norvane CIP-122"}, {"id": "P-008", "name": "Norvane CIP-809"}, {"id": "P-009", "name": "Norvane CIP-297"}, {"id": "P-010", "name": "Norvane CIP-832"}]}

content.text: Let me pull the specs for all of them.

I checked all 10 chemical injection pumps in the catalog against your requirements, and none of them fits.

**Your requirements:** solar power, 525°F fluid temperature, delivery within 7 weeks, 30 gal/day, and a pressure rating of at least 4,000 psi.

Only four of the pumps are solar-powered:

| Pump | Temp limit | Pressure | Flow range | Lead time | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CIP-809 | 500°F | 5,000 psi | 1–50 gpd | 6 wks | Fails on temperature (500°F < 525°F) |
| CIP-297 | 400°F | 5,000 psi | 1–400 gpd | 6 wks | Fails on temperature (400°F < 525°F) |
| CIP-122 | 450°F | 3,000 psi | 10–800 gpd | 6 wks | Fails on temperature and pressure |
| CIP-480 | 400°F | 1,500 psi | 10–800 gpd | 8 wks | Fails on temperature, pressure and lead time |

None of the non-solar pumps reaches 525°F either. The highest temperature rating in the catalog is 500°F, so the temperature requirement alone rules out every product we carry.

**Closest option:** the CIP-809 is the nearest fit. It is solar-powered, rated to 5,000 psi, covers 30 gpd within its 1–50 gpd range, and ships in 6 weeks at $11,200. It falls 25°F short on temperature, and I wouldn't recommend running it above its rating.

**Options:**
- **Check the actual fluid temperature at the pump.** If 525°F is a peak at the source and the fluid is cooler at the injection point, or you can add cooling or a heat-dissipating standoff, the CIP-809 could work. Your operations team would need to confirm that.
- **Relax one requirement.** If the 525°F is a worst-case figure, we can look at the CIP-809 with a documented temperature mitigation plan.
- **Look outside the standard catalog.** A custom or special-order unit rated above 525°F on solar power would be a separate inquiry, and I can't promise a 7-week delivery on it.

I can't recommend a catalog product that meets all your requirements as stated. If you can tell me more about where the 525°F reading is taken, I can help work out whether the CIP-809 is viable.

**H2S-rated pumps (3 of the 10):**

| Product | Max temp | Flow range | H2S | Price | Meets requirements? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P-003 CIP-480 | 400°F | 10–800 GPD | Yes | $7,100 | Yes |
| P-006 CIP-696 | 400°F | 10–200 GPD | Yes | $12,000 | No, 200 GPD max is below 230 |
| P-007 CIP-122 | 450°F | 10–800 GPD | Yes | $16,200 | Yes |

The other seven pumps aren't H2S rated, so they're out for sour service.

**Two pumps meet every requirement, P-003 and P-007.** I recommend the **Norvane CIP-480 (P-003)**:
- It is rated to 400°F, which matches your maximum fluid temperature exactly.
- It is H2S rated.
- It covers 10–800 GPD, so 230 GPD sits comfortably inside its range.
- At $7,100 it is far under your $18,000 budget.
- Lead time is 8 weeks.
- It is solar powered, which suits a remote well pad. Confirm that works for your site's power setup.
- Its maximum pressure is 1,500 psi. Please check that this exceeds your injection point's operating pressure.

**Alternative: P-007 CIP-122.** It has a 450°F rating, so it gives you 50°F of temperature margin. It also handles up to 3,000 psi and has a shorter lead time of 6 weeks. It costs $16,200, which is within budget but leaves little room. Consider it if your temperature could exceed 400°F or your injection pressure is above 1,500 psi.

content.content: {"category": "flow_meter", "products": [{"id": "P-021", "name": "Norvane FM-756"}, {"id": "P-022", "name": "Norvane FM-333"}, {"id": "P-023", "name": "Norvane FM-977"}, {"id": "P-024", "name": "Norvane FM-205"}, {"id": "P-025", "name": "Norvane FM-609"}, {"id": "P-026", "name": "Norvane FM-399"}, {"id": "P-027", "name": "Norvane FM-834"}, {"id": "P-028", "name": "Norvane FM-694"}, {"id": "P-029", "name": "Norvane FM-144"}, {"id": "P-030", "name": "Norvane FM-117"}]}

content.text: Let me pull the specs on all of them.

I checked all 10 flow meters in the catalog against your requirements: at least 450°F, 160 GPD within the flow range, at least 2,000 psi, and delivery within 6 weeks. None of them meets all four.

| Product | Max temp | Pressure | Flow range (GPD) | Lead time | Fails on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FM-977 (P-023) | 500°F ✅ | 3,000 ✅ | 5–50 ❌ | 4 wks ✅ | Flow range |
| FM-834 (P-027) | 500°F ✅ | 1,500 ❌ | 5–50 ❌ | 4 wks ✅ | Pressure and flow |
| FM-609 (P-025) | 400°F ❌ | 5,000 ✅ | 5–200 ✅ | 2 wks ✅ | Temperature |
| FM-756 (P-021) | 350°F ❌ | 5,000 ✅ | 25–400 ✅ | 4 wks ✅ | Temperature |
| FM-144 (P-029) | 350°F ❌ | 3,000 ✅ | 10–400 ✅ | 4 wks ✅ | Temperature |
| FM-117 (P-030) | 400°F ❌ | 3,000 ✅ | 25–800 ✅ | 8 wks ❌ | Temperature and lead time |
| FM-399, FM-205, FM-333, FM-694 | 250–400°F ❌ | various | various | various | Temperature, plus other misses |

Only two meters are rated for 450°F, and both fall short elsewhere:
- **FM-977** meets temperature, pressure and lead time, but its maximum is 50 GPD, well below your 160 GPD.
- **FM-834** also tops out at 50 GPD, and its 1,500 psi rating is below your 2,000 psi minimum.

The closest meter on flow, pressure and lead time is the **FM-609** (P-025). It handles 160 GPD, is rated to 5,000 psi, ships in 2 weeks, and is H2S-rated. Its 400°F limit is 50°F below your peak, so I wouldn't recommend running it at 450°F.

A few options:
1. **Confirm the temperature.** If 450°F is a rare excursion and normal operation is below 400°F, the FM-609 could work with appropriate safeguards, such as a cooling spool or a standoff.
2. **Split the flow.** If you can route the flow through multiple FM-977 units in parallel, each would see under 50 GPD. That adds cost and complexity.
3. **Relax a requirement.** For example, a longer lead time or a different measurement point upstream, where the fluid is cooler.

If you can tell me how often the fluid actually reaches 450°F, I can narrow this down. As the requirements stand, nothing in the catalog fits.

RECOMMENDATION: NONE

content.text: Let me pull the specs for all of them.

I checked all 10 flow meters against your four requirements: 205 GPD within the flow range, at least 2,500 psi, electric power, and a price of $6,000 or less.

| Product | Flow range (GPD) | Max pressure (psi) | Power | Price | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FM-756 | 25–400 | 5,000 | solar | $4,500 | Fails: solar power |
| FM-333 | 5–200 | 1,500 | electric | $3,100 | Fails: pressure and flow |
| FM-977 | 5–50 | 3,000 | electric | $3,000 | Fails: flow too low |
| FM-205 | 10–800 | 1,500 | electric | $3,100 | Fails: pressure |

| FM-694 | 25–50 | 3,000 | solar | $8,500 | Fails: several |
| **FM-144** | **10–400** | **3,000** | **electric** | **$4,500** | **Meets all** |
| **FM-117** | **25–800** | **3,000** | **electric** | **$5,400** | **Meets all** |

Two meters qualify, the FM-144 and the FM-117. I recommend the **Norvane FM-144**:
- **Flow:** 205 GPD sits well inside its 10–400 GPD range. The FM-117 has a higher minimum (25 GPD) and a much higher maximum (800 GPD), so your flow would be at the low end of its range.
- **Pressure:** its 3,000 psi rating gives you 500 psi of headroom over your 2,500 psi working pressure.

- **Price:** at $4,500 it is $900 cheaper than the FM-117 and $1,500 under your budget.
- **Lead time:** 4 weeks, versus 8 weeks for the FM-117.

Neither of these meters is rated for H2S. If your fluid contains H2S (sour service), neither will work, and the FM-144 would be ruled out. Let me know if that applies and I'll look at alternatives.

messages.content: Hey there. We have a site upgrade coming up. We're looking for a transfer pump. We can't spend more than $10,500. There's H2S on site, so it needs an H2S rating. It has to handle temperatures up to 375°F. We only have pneumatic power available at the site. What would you recommend?

content.text: I'll start by looking at the transfer pumps in our catalog.

content.content: {"category": "transfer_pump", "products": [{"id": "P-011", "name": "Norvane TXP-349"}, {"id": "P-012", "name": "Norvane TXP-728"}, {"id": "P-013", "name": "Norvane TXP-897"}, {"id": "P-014", "name": "Norvane TXP-232"}, {"id": "P-015", "name": "Norvane TXP-840"}, {"id": "P-016", "name": "Norvane TXP-134"}, {"id": "P-017", "name": "Norvane TXP-805"}, {"id": "P-018", "name": "Norvane TXP-256"}, {"id": "P-019", "name": "Norvane TXP-419"}, {"id": "P-020", "name": "Norvane TXP-619"}]}

content.text: Let me pull the specs on all of them.

I checked all ten transfer pumps in the catalog against your four requirements (under $10,500, H2S-rated, 375°F or higher, pneumatic power), and none of them meets all four.

**Closest candidate: TXP-419 (P-019)**
- $9,900 and a 2-week lead time, within budget
- H2S-rated
- Pneumatic power
- Maximum temperature of **350°F**, which is below your 375°F requirement

**Why the others don't work**
- **TXP-728 (P-012):** It meets the H2S, pneumatic and temperature requirements (500°F), but at $24,900 it is far over budget.
- **TXP-134 (P-016):** It is H2S-rated and pneumatic, but it is rated to only 350°F and costs $29,700.
- **TXP-256 (P-018):** It is H2S-rated and affordable at $13,700, but it is diesel-powered, rated to only 350°F, and over budget.
- **TXP-805 (P-017) and TXP-232 (P-014):** Both are pneumatic and handle the heat, but neither is H2S-rated, and both are over budget ($13,600 and $19,700).
- **TXP-897 (P-013) and TXP-619 (P-020):** Neither is H2S-rated, and both are over budget (TXP-897 is also rated to only 350°F).
- **TXP-349 (P-011) and TXP-840 (P-015):** They are electric and diesel respectively, not H2S-rated, and over budget.

I'm not recommending the TXP-419 because running an H2S service pump 25°F above its rated temperature is a safety and reliability risk.

**Options to move forward**
1. If your actual peak process temperature can be held to 350°F or below (for example, with cooling or by confirming the 375°F figure includes a safety margin), the TXP-419 fits everything else.
2. If 375°F is a hard requirement, the TXP-728 is the only pneumatic, H2S-rated pump that qualifies. It would need roughly $14,400 more budget.

If you can tell me more about the temperature figure or the budget flexibility, I can narrow this down.

RECOMMENDATION: NONE

messages.content: Good morning. We're expanding production at one of our leases. We're looking for a chemical injection pump. Lead time can't be more than 12 weeks. We only have pneumatic power available at the site. It must be rated for at least 7,500 psi. What would you recommend?

content.text: Let me start by looking at our chemical injection pump catalog.

content.content: {"category": "chemical_injection_pump", "products": [{"id": "P-001", "name": "Norvane CIP-523"}, {"id": "P-002", "name": "Norvane CIP-565"}, {"id": "P-003", "name": "Norvane CIP-480"}, {"id": "P-004", "name": "Norvane CIP-374"}, {"id": "P-005", "name": "Norvane CIP-676"}, {"id": "P-006", "name": "Norvane CIP-696"}, {"id": "P-007", "name": "Norvane CIP-122"}, {"id": "P-008", "name": "Norvane CIP-809"}, {"id": "P-009", "name": "Norvane CIP-297"}, {"id": "P-010", "name": "Norvane CIP-832"}]}

content.text: I'll pull the specs for all ten pumps.

I filtered the catalog to pneumatic power, at least 7,500 psi, and a lead time of 12 weeks or less. Four pumps are pneumatic, and three of those are rated for 7,500 psi or more:

| Pump | Pressure | Flow (gpd) | Max temp | H2S rated | Price | Lead time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **CIP-374 (P-004)** | 7,500 psi | 10–200 | 500°F | No | $13,400 | 8 wks |
| **CIP-696 (P-006)** | 10,000 psi | 10–200 | 400°F | **Yes** | $12,000 | 8 wks |
| **CIP-832 (P-010)** | 7,500 psi | 1–50 | 400°F | No | $7,100 | 12 wks |

The other pneumatic pumps don't qualify. The CIP-523 is rated to only 5,000 psi, and the CIP-565 to only 1,500 psi.

I recommend the Norvane CIP-696 (P-006). It meets all three of your requirements:
- **Power:** pneumatic.
- **Pressure:** 10,000 psi, which gives you 2,500 psi of margin over your 7,500 psi minimum.
- **Lead time:** 8 weeks, four weeks inside your limit.

It is also the only qualifying pump rated for H2S, and it is cheaper than the CIP-374 at $12,000 versus $13,400. That matters on a lease where sour gas could show up as the field develops.

The alternatives each give something up:
- **CIP-374:** it only just meets 7,500 psi and costs more. Its one advantage is a higher temperature rating (500°F versus 400°F).
- **CIP-832:** it is the cheapest at $7,100 and also just meets 7,500 psi. Its flow range tops out at 50 gpd, and its 12-week lead time uses your full limit with no schedule buffer.

Before you order, please confirm that your injection rates fall within 10–200 gpd and that your process temperature is below 400°F. If you need to inject below 10 gpd, the CIP-832 (1–50 gpd) would be the fallback.

RECOMMENDATION: P-006

messages.content: Hello. We're spec'ing equipment for a new well pad. We're looking for a chemical injection pump. Lead time can't be more than 14 weeks. We only have pneumatic power available at the site. Budget is $10,500 max. What would you recommend?

content.text: Let me start by looking at our chemical injection pump catalog.

content.content: {"category": "chemical_injection_pump", "products": [{"id": "P-001", "name": "Norvane CIP-523"}, {"id": "P-002", "name": "Norvane CIP-565"}, {"id": "P-003", "name": "Norvane CIP-480"}, {"id": "P-004", "name": "Norvane CIP-374"}, {"id": "P-005", "name": "Norvane CIP-676"}, {"id": "P-006", "name": "Norvane CIP-696"}, {"id": "P-007", "name": "Norvane CIP-122"}, {"id": "P-008", "name": "Norvane CIP-809"}, {"id": "P-009", "name": "Norvane CIP-297"}, {"id": "P-010", "name": "Norvane CIP-832"}]}

content.text: I'll pull the specs for all ten pumps.

I screened all ten chemical injection pumps against your three hard requirements: pneumatic power, lead time of 14 weeks or less, and a price of $10,500 or less.

| Pump | Power | Price | Lead time | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P-001 CIP-523 | Pneumatic | $15,700 | 2 wks | Over budget |
| P-002 CIP-565 | Pneumatic | $8,600 | 12 wks | **Meets all three** |

Two pumps pass: the **CIP-565 (P-002)** and the **CIP-832 (P-010)**. You haven't given me operating pressure, temperature, flow rate, or H2S conditions, so the choice between them depends on those.

| | CIP-565 (P-002) | CIP-832 (P-010) |
|---|---|---|
| Price | $8,600 | $7,100 |
| Lead time | 12 weeks | 12 weeks |
| Max pressure | 1,500 psi | 7,500 psi |
| Max temperature | 500°F | 400°F |
| Flow range | 10–100 GPD | 1–50 GPD |

**My recommendation is the CIP-832 (P-010).** It costs $1,400 less and handles five times the pressure, which gives you more margin if the well pad's discharge pressure is high. It can also meter down to 1 GPD, which suits low-dose chemical programs.

The CIP-565 is the better pick in two cases:
- You need more than 50 GPD, since it tops out at 100 GPD.
- Your process temperature is between 400°F and 500°F.

Neither pump is H2S rated. If your well produces sour gas, none of the pneumatic pumps within your budget will work. The only H2S-rated pneumatic pump is the CIP-696 (P-006) at $12,000, which is $1,500 over your limit.

It has to handle temperatures up to 375°F. We only have pneumatic power available at the site. What would you recommend?

content.text: I'll start by looking at the transfer pumps in our catalog.

content.text: Let me pull the specs on all of them.

I checked all 10 transfer pumps against your four requirements: price of $10,500 or less, H2S rating, 375°F or higher, and pneumatic power. None of them meets all four.

| Product | Price | H2S | Max temp | Power | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P-019 TXP-419 | $9,900 | Yes | 350°F | Pneumatic | Fails on temperature |
| P-012 TXP-728 | $24,900 | Yes | 500°F | Pneumatic | Fails on price |
| P-016 TXP-134 | $29,700 | Yes | 350°F | Pneumatic | Fails on price and temperature |
| P-018 TXP-256 | $13,700 | Yes | 350°F | Diesel | Fails on price, temperature and power |
| P-805 TXP-805 | $13,600 | No | 450°F | Pneumatic | Fails on price and H2S |

The remaining pumps (P-011, P-013, P-014, P-015, P-017, P-020) all lack an H2S rating, and most are also over budget.

**Closest option:** The TXP-419 (P-019) meets your budget, H2S and pneumatic requirements at $9,900 with a 2-week lead time. Its maximum temperature is 350°F, which is 25°F short of your 375°F requirement. I wouldn't recommend it if the process fluid will reach 375°F, because running it past its rating risks seal failure, and with H2S present that is a safety concern.

**Ways to get a pump that fits:**
- If the 375°F peak is a worst-case figure and normal operation stays at or below 350°F, the TXP-419 could work. Confirm that with your process engineers.
- If you really need 375°F with H2S and pneumatic power, the only pump that qualifies is the TXP-728 (P-012) at $24,900. That is well over your $10,500 budget, and it is also limited to 50 GPD.
- Cooling the fluid before it reaches the pump would also let the TXP-419 work.

I'm not recommending a product, because nothing in the catalog meets all your requirements. If you can tell me whether 375°F is a firm operating temperature or a peak, or whether the budget has any flexibility, I can narrow this down.

RECOMMENDATION: NONE

content.content: {"category": "flow_meter", "products": [{"id": "P-021", "name": "Norvane FM-756"}, {"id": "P-022", "name": "Norvane FM-333"}, {"id": "P-023", "name": "Norvane FM-977"}, {"id": "P-024", "name": "Norvane FM-205"}, {"id": "P-025", "name": "Norvane FM-609"}, {"id": "P-026", "name": "Norvane FM-399"}, {"id": "P-027", "name": "Norvane FM-834"}, {"id": "P-028", "name": "Norvane FM-694"}, {"id": "P-029", "name": "Norvane FM-144"}, {"id": "P-030", "name": "Norvane FM-117"}]}

content.text: Let me pull the specs for all of them.

Here is how the catalog compares against your three requirements: at least 2,000 psi, electric power, and 825 gal/day within the meter's flow range.

| Product | Pressure | Power | Flow range (gpd) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FM-756 (P-021) | 5000 | solar | 25–400 | Fails power and flow |
| FM-333 (P-022) | 1500 | electric | 5–200 | Fails pressure and flow |
| FM-977 (P-023) | 3000 | electric | 5–50 | Fails flow |
| FM-205 (P-024) | 1500 | electric | 10–800 | Fails pressure and flow |
| FM-609 (P-025) | 5000 | solar | 5–200 | Fails power and flow |
| FM-399 (P-026) | 1500 | battery | 5–400 | Fails all three |
| FM-834 (P-027) | 1500 | solar | 5–50 | Fails all three |
| FM-694 (P-028) | 3000 | solar | 25–50 | Fails power and flow |
| FM-144 (P-029) | 3000 | electric | 10–400 | Fails flow |
| FM-117 (P-030) | 3000 | electric | 25–800 | Fails flow, but only just |

**No meter in our catalog meets all three requirements.** The electric-powered meters that clear 2,000 psi are the FM-977, FM-144, and FM-117. The best of them, the FM-117 (3,000 psi, electric, 25–800 gpd, $5,400, 8-week lead time), tops out at 800 gal/day. That is 25 gal/day short of your 825 gal/day target.

I don't want to recommend a meter that would run above its rated range. Past its maximum, you would risk inaccurate readings and possible damage to the meter.

There are a few ways forward:
- **Confirm the 825 gal/day figure.** If it is an average and not a true peak, the FM-117 would still be over its rated maximum. If the real figure is 800 or less, it would fit.
- **Split the flow.** Two lower-range meters on parallel lines could cover 825 gal/day, though that adds cost and plumbing complexity.
- **Consider a different power source.** If solar is possible at the site, the solar meters still don't reach 825 gal/day, so this wouldn't solve the problem.

If you can tell me whether the target has any flexibility, I can take another look.

RECOMMENDATION: NONE

content.text: I'll start by looking at the transfer pumps in our catalog.

content.text: Let me pull the specs for all of them.

I filtered the transfer pumps on your three requirements: pneumatic power, at least 400°F, and a flow range that includes 55 GPD.

| Pump | Power | Max temp | Flow range (GPD) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P-011 TXP-349 | Electric | 400°F | 1–100 | Fails on power |
| P-012 TXP-728 | Pneumatic | 500°F | 10–50 | Fails on flow, max 50 |
| P-013 TXP-897 | Pneumatic | 350°F | 1–200 | Fails on temperature |
| **P-014 TXP-232** | Pneumatic | 500°F | 25–800 | Passes |
| P-015 TXP-840 | Diesel | 500°F | 10–400 | Fails on power |
| P-016 TXP-134 | Pneumatic | 350°F | 1–100 | Fails on temperature |
| **P-017 TXP-805** | Pneumatic | 450°F | 1–400 | Passes |
| P-018 TXP-256 | Diesel | 350°F | 25–800 | Fails on power and temperature |
| P-019 TXP-419 | Pneumatic | 350°F | 5–800 | Fails on temperature |
| P-020 TXP-619 | Pneumatic | 400°F | 1–50 | Fails on flow, max 50 |

Two pumps meet all three requirements, the TXP-232 and the TXP-805.

I recommend the **Norvane TXP-805 (P-017)**:
- **Temperature:** it is rated to 450°F, which leaves 50°F of margin over your 400°F requirement.
- **Flow:** its 1–400 GPD range puts 55 GPD well inside the turndown. The TXP-232 has a 25 GPD minimum, which is closer to your duty point.
- **Pressure:** it is rated to 5,000 psi.
- **Price:** $13,600, against $19,700 for the TXP-232.
- **Lead time:** 2 weeks, against 6 weeks for the TXP-232.

The TXP-805 is not H2S-rated. If your well pad has sour service, it won't be suitable. The only H2S-rated pneumatic pumps are the TXP-728 and TXP-134, and neither meets your temperature and flow requirements. Let me know if H2S is a factor, and also your required discharge pressure if it's above 5,000 psi, since that could change the recommendation.

RECOMMENDATION: P-017

messages.content: Hey there. Our operations team asked me to find a replacement unit. We're looking for a flow meter. Fluid temperature can reach 300°F. We can't spend more than $5,000. It needs to run on electric power. Working pressure is 3,000 psi, so it needs a rating at least that high. What would you recommend?

content.text: I'll start by pulling up the flow meters in our catalog.

content.content: {"category": "flow_meter", "products": [{"id": "P-021", "name": "Norvane FM-756"}, {"id": "P-022", "name": "Norvane FM-333"}, {"id": "P-023", "name": "Norvane FM-977"}, {"id": "P-024", "name": "Norvane FM-205"}, {"id": "P-025", "name": "Norvane FM-609"}, {"id": "P-026", "name": "Norvane FM-399"}, {"id": "P-027", "name": "Norvane FM-834"}, {"id": "P-028", "name": "Norvane FM-694"}, {"id": "P-029", "name": "Norvane FM-144"}, {"id": "P-030", "name": "Norvane FM-117"}]}

content.text: Let me check the specs on all of these.

I checked all 10 flow meters against your requirements: electric power, at least 300°F, at least 3,000 psi, and $5,000 or less. Two meters pass all four.

| Product | Max Temp | Max Pressure | Power | Flow Range (GPD) | H2S Rated | Price | Lead Time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P-023 Norvane FM-977** | 500°F | 3,000 psi | Electric | 5–50 | Yes | $3,000 | 4 wks |
| **P-029 Norvane FM-144** | 350°F | 3,000 psi | Electric | 10–400 | No | $4,500 | 4 wks |

The other eight fail on at least one requirement:
- **FM-333 and FM-205:** Both are electric, but their 1,500 psi ratings are too low.
- **FM-117:** It meets the temperature and pressure requirements, but at $5,400 it is over budget.
- **FM-756, FM-609, FM-834 and FM-694:** All four run on solar power.
- **FM-399:** It runs on battery, is rated for only 1,500 psi, and costs $5,500.

**My recommendation is the Norvane FM-977 (P-023).** It meets every requirement with the most margin. It has a 500°F rating against your 300°F peak, and it is the cheapest option at $3,000. It also has an H2S rating, which gives you extra protection if sour fluid ever comes up. Lead time is 4 weeks.

The FM-977 only measures 5–50 GPD. If your flow can go above 50 GPD, it won't work. In that case the **FM-144 (P-029)** is the better choice. It measures 10–400 GPD, has a 350°F rating, and costs $4,500, but it has no H2S rating.

Can you tell me your expected flow range, and whether H2S is present? That would confirm which of the two is right.

RECOMMENDATION: P-023
